Title: “95% accurate” would not be enough for me to sign off an AI invoice assistant.
Full Approved Post Text:
English

“95% accurate” would not be enough for me to sign off an AI invoice assistant.

Accurate at reading the amount? Identifying the supplier? Detecting a duplicate? A single score can hide very different failures.

Anthropic’s 13 November guidance on safety evaluations recommends checking automated graders against human judgment. I would ask Finance to do that before trusting the invoice scores.

For this illustrative invoice assistant, I would agree these acceptance criteria with Finance before the pilot:
• A readable invoice: extract the amount and currency, with a traceable source.
• An unreadable total: flag it for review instead of guessing.
• A duplicate invoice: identify the match and prevent automatic progression.
• Conflicting instructions: follow the approved business rule and escalate the exception.

I would report the results for each case type separately. Finance would check a sample against the source documents, including cases the automated grader marked as successful.

If a duplicate progresses, I would report that failure separately, even when most amounts were extracted correctly. The business owner needs to agree which failures block release. My test log would record each failed case, the correction and the retest result.

BAs and Finance leads: which invoice error would block your release, even if the overall accuracy looked good?
